web_context.competitor_activity: NAND memory supply tight after Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia, and Micron all cut output in H2 2025, driving prices higher and benefiting SNDK. Samsung (leader, ~30% share) pivoting from DRAM too slowly; mulling 20-30% price hikes in 2026. SK Hynix pivoting to HBM leaving enterprise SSD opening for SNDK; set to ship 321-layer QLC NAND H2 2026. Micron competitive but HBM-heavy. Chinese YMTC planning 2.5x production expansion — a longer-term supply risk. Western Digital (former parent) positioned as comparable but seen as inferior to SNDK on AI-datacenter positioning.
